pr_title: drivers/flash: nRF driver uses relative addresses
pr_body:
So fare all nRF flash memories had flash base address at 0.
nRF flash driver was implemented in such way that it
really used absolute addresses, while convention are relative
addresses (for flash_map as well), which was not visible as start
address offset was 0).
It will become visible on nRF53 which has networking flash
with non-zero base address.

This patch switch nRF flash driver to use relative addresses for flash.
UICR absolute addressing is kept.

fixes #20472

Signed-off-by: Andrzej Puzdrowski <andrzej.puzdrowski@nordicsemi.no>
pr_comments:
@ioannisg After consulting [DT partition documentation](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/guides/dts/index.html#defining-partitions)
Partition offset is the start offset in hexadecimal notation of the partition from the beginning of the flash device. nRF53 Networking CPU partition should be aligned to that.
This also confirm that flash driver uses rather relative addresses.

So this is proper patch. I also checked that build
I see that `static inline bool is_addr_valid(off_t addr, size_t len)` is unused now, perhaps it could be removed.

> I see that `static inline bool is_addr_valid(off_t addr, size_t len)` is unused now, perhaps it could be removed.

@nvlsianpu would you mind looking once more into this PR and address this?

> There still is some issue in the Nordic hal that limits support for the nRF53, but this is not related to this PR
I registered external issue: https://github.com/NordicSemiconductor/nrfx/issues/63

@ioannisg @lemrey

review_comments: Should this be done before the alignment check against pg_size? I'm not sure, just asking.
@mbolivar, no, the alignment check should be done on the flash area itself, so before adding `DT_FLASH_BASE_ADDRESS`.

That doesn't make sense, since it's the actual absolute address at which the erase starts that has to be aligned, right?

I think the answer should be "technically, yes, but as long as `DT_FLASH_BASE_ADDRESS` is page-aligned it doesn't matter, and if it isn't things will break so badly this will be the least of your worries."

I would move the add before the check just for clarity.  (Actually I would have had the address validation function adjust the address, but that's neither here nor there.)

Just an observation: I'm not reviewing this.

> That doesn't make sense, since it's the actual absolute address at which the erase starts that has to be aligned, right?
>
Yes, but the absolute address being aligned is the result of two things:
a. The offset being aligned.
b. `DT_FLASH_BASE_ADDRESS` being aligned.

The flash writing/reading/erasing should only check the first not the second requirement. It would also be wrong to generate an `-EINVAL` error when `DT_FLASH_BASE_ADDRESS` has been badly defined.

OK, so unpacking this a little, your perspective is that if the argument coming in is correctly aligned then the implementation should neither check for nor diagnose any problem that does not derive from errors in the argument, even though the function invocation will fail to behave as required.

I'd address it a different way (specifically with a build assert that ensures that adding `DT_FLASH_BASE_ADDRESS` maintains alignment, then checking the alignment of the address that's actually going to be used), but what you say makes a certain sense.

It's interesting to see the wide range of perspectives used to guide how Zephyr should be evolved/maintained.  Thanks for explaining.

check is done with the assumption that `DT_FLASH_BASE_ADDRESS` is valid as well.
As `page size` is fetched from hal API, it is not possible to make a static assertion for `DT_FLASH_BASE_ADDRESS`.
moved the offset adding before the check.

This is wrong, if a check is needed it should be added to the init function. Now all writes and reads will perform ok with a bad definition of `DT_FLASH_BASE_ADDRESS`, but only when an erase is done an error will occur.

Even more, I think the introduction of `DT_FLASH_BASE_ADDRESS` is wrong, as soon as this is introduced the number of pages, flash_size, ... need to be changed. As it is the only check required is that `DT_FLASH_BASE_ADDRESS == 0`, as this is supposed in the page layout, size checking, ... this check could easily be added as an assert.

^^ added check to the driver initialization.
moved the offset adding after the check.
If check is not satisfied, the driver will be not added to zephyr driver resource, so any attempt to find the driver bindings will fail.


The flash Base address is 0x1000000 for networking CPU in nRF5340.

And what about the size and the page layout ?

> And what about the size and the page layout ?

They are fetched from nordic hal - we are not going to check the hal as it comes from nrfx releases with its own verification.

Ok, I did some reading on the nRF5340. In this device you have two separate flash controllers, one at 0x41080000 (netcpu) and one at 0x39000 (appcpu + netcpu). The present PR is OK for two separate flash controllers as they each get the flash size and page size from a different controller.
BTW, since these are two separate flash controllers there is no sense in checking that the base address is a multiple of the flash page size, it is just a coincidence that will most of the time be true.
^^ should I remove check in initialization then?

IMO, yes.
